title: Shortest path through a floor plan
prompt:
grid is a list of equal-length strings: "." is open floor and "#" is a wall. Moving one cell up, down, left or right costs one step. Return the fewest steps from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell, or -1 if it cannot be reached (including when either cell is a wall).

- 1 to 300 rows and 1 to 300 columns.
- A 1×1 open grid needs 0 steps.
hints: Every move costs the same. Which traversal finds shortest paths in an unweighted graph?
Breadth-first search from (0, 0) reaches cells in order of distance.
Store distance per cell, mark cells visited when you enqueue them, and use a head index instead of shift() so the queue stays O(1).

solution.explanation: Treat each open cell as a node with edges to open neighbours. BFS visits nodes in nondecreasing distance, so the first time a cell is reached is via a shortest path. Marking on enqueue prevents duplicates in the queue.

complexity.notes: Each cell is enqueued at most once and checks four neighbours. Array.shift() is O(n) in JavaScript, which is why the queue uses a head index.

followUps: Some cells cost 2 to cross. What replaces BFS?
How would A* with Manhattan distance speed up large grids?
